scene.summary: An intermittent alarm cuts the quiet. It asks what changed; it does not authorise a shock or an airway swap.

dialogue.speaker: Circulation lead
dialogue.line: Alarm first. Indication second. Readiness is not a green light.

captions: Intermittent tone. Fragile pulse still present. No energy values displayed.

clinicalTruth.breathing: Ventilation continues; chest movement still needs deliberate check against the alarm context.
clinicalTruth.circulation: Frequent ectopy with intermittent alarm; defibrillator may be prepared without creating indication.
clinicalTruth.communicationAccess: WAIT still active; emergency vocabulary available if access later becomes contested.

visibleEvidence.label: Alarm as question
visibleEvidence.detail: The tone starts a workup. It does not name the cause.

visibleEvidence.label: Transport held
visibleEvidence.detail: Movement off the bay remains held while suction endurance is unresolved.

visibleEvidence.label: Defibrillator may be prepared
visibleEvidence.detail: Preparing equipment is not the same as deciding to use it.

hiddenState.primaryCause: Still unproven. External load and circuit geometry remain candidates.
notes: Keep cause hidden through the first alarm window.

communicationBeat.note: Alarm pressure does not cancel WAIT for non-emergency questions.

familyBeat.note: Family may track questions aloud; they do not interpret clinical signals as staff.

exitConditions.description: Pressure opens a short resource-allocation window while transport stays held.
